purpose: Cover every acceptance criterion of US-18904 with one node:test case each in test/discovery/journey-review.test.js; DEFINE lands the named declarations flagged not yet built so the strict coverage audit binds each criterion, and BUILD (FBS-213) removes the flags as it makes them pass.
title: US-18904 UX intake gate suite (journey-review)

testCases.description: [happy] Given a journey that passes every structural check, when the journey review verb runs with --by and a name, then ReviewStamp.state equals "reviewed", ReviewStamp.by equals the name, ReviewStamp.at carries the time and the discoveryHash of the record, and ReviewStamp.wireframeHashes carries one sha256 per screen with a wireframe.
testCases.testPointer: test/discovery/journey-review.test.js::AC-18904-1 happy: a journey that passes every structural check

testCases.description: [happy] Given a reviewed record, when discovery:reviewed evaluates with the record and every wireframe file unchanged, then it passes, and the review verb that produced the stamp printed the one-line summary (journeys, steps, screens, interruptions mapped) before writing.
[failure] Given a journey that fails any structural check, when the journey review verb runs, then it exits 4 printing the failing checks and writes no ReviewStamp.
testCases.testPointer: test/discovery/journey-review.test.js::AC-18904-3 failure: a journey that fails any structural check

testCases.description: [edge] Given a reviewed record, when a wireframe file's bytes change or a journey source is re-minted, then discovery:reviewed fails as stale with a why naming the changed screens or journey, and a second review at the new hash makes it pass again.

[must-not] Given the managed agent-instructions block, when rcf init or rcf doctor --fix writes it, then it carries the rule that the harness never runs the journey review verb on its own beside the ADR-4132 prototype rule, and no verb other than journey review ever writes ReviewStamp.
